question.problem:
Given the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$, which of the following vectors are orthogonal to $u?$

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
We compute the dot product between $u$ and each of the listed vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =0\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 4+3\cdot (-2)+2\cdot 5 \\  & =0-4-6+10 \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot w & ={u}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {w}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {w}_{4} \\  & =0\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 2+3\cdot 0+2\cdot 1 \\  & =0-2+0+2 \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot x & ={u}_{1}\cdot {x}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {x}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {x}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {x}_{4} \\  & =0\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 1+3\cdot (-3)+2\cdot (-2) \\  & =0-1-9-4 \\  & =-14.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the correct option is $v$ and $w$ only.
